topic: football, sports science, and physics learning through gameplay
audience: young sports-curious learners (9–15), parents, and educators

comparables.title: Ronaldo vs My Unbeatable Goalie Robot
comparables.audience_fit: Official science-and-engineering creator; family and student audience is supported by the channel subject and independent 8+ audience guidance.
comparables.topic_fit: Football action joined to a real engineering demonstration; direct subject overlap with football and physics learning.
observed_type_traits: No added display lettering visible in the inspected thumbnail.
Real athlete and physical robot provide the hierarchy.
Natural stadium colors and photo detail; no drawn arrow or glow treatment.
comparables.feed_size_behavior: At 320x180 the player/robot contrast and central physical subject remain legible; there is no small headline to decode.
comparables.decision_reason: Use as a topic-native composition and restraint comparator, not as evidence that any particular font or copy performs.

comparables.title: 20 YouTubers Compete in Biggest Trick Shot Contest Ever! | TSWC ’25
comparables.audience_fit: Official family-friendly sports-entertainment channel; directly relevant to youth sports viewing.
comparables.topic_fit: Football-adjacent physical challenge and trick-shot competition; strong audience context, looser physics-learning fit.
observed_type_traits: No added display lettering visible in the inspected thumbnail.
Real people and target activity carry the story.
Natural photo treatment and clear subject hierarchy; no procedural arrow.
comparables.feed_size_behavior: At 320x180 the face and action grouping remain recognizable; the image does not depend on fine text.
comparables.decision_reason: Use as a youth-sports audience and scene-first comparator; do not transfer the group collage or creator identity.

selected_style.family: Inter, a contemporary neutral sans-serif already bundled with Portfolio
selected_style.weight: 800; one line; restrained tracking; four words maximum
selected_style.case: uppercase for short-form scanability, without condensed or arcade letterforms
selected_style.color: warm white over the calm navy dusk region; no gradient fill
selected_style.effects: no outline, glow, bevel, extrusion, trajectory, arrow, or decorative curve; only a small soft shadow for local contrast
selected_style.placement: upper-left calm sky, outside the actual gameplay proof and player/ball focal area

rejected_styles.style: condensed black arcade display with gold-orange gradient, stroke, glow, rings, and impact vectors
rejected_styles.reason: No matching type treatment appears in either current topic comparator; it would repeat the rejected dated game-poster direction and compete with real product proof.

rejected_styles.style: default-font caption pasted beside a rectangular screenshot
rejected_styles.reason: Creates a generic split-card template and separates the teaching idea from the action.

rejected_styles.style: creator-logo, reaction face, fabricated score, or drawn trajectory
rejected_styles.reason: Not needed to explain the actual product pixels and risks implying evidence or identity that is not present.

selection_logic: Both selected official YouTube comparables are topic/audience adjacent and omit added display text. Their common signal is that real activity carries the thumbnail at feed size. The selected four-word neutral-sans line is a deliberately restrained editorial cue, not a claimed winning font; the real KickLab screenshot remains the sole product-proof layer. Comparable views and likes are captured context only and have zero typography-performance weight.

performance_evidence.baseline_method: Required baseline: median 30-day views for at least four recent standard-length videos on the same channel, normalized by each video age and matched for topic/audience; exclude Shorts and sponsored outliers.
performance_evidence.formula: matched-style comparable views normalized per day / same-channel baseline views normalized per day; require at least 4 matched-style examples and ratio >= 1.5
performance_evidence.limitation: Available public view/like counts do not isolate typography from topic, title, audience, or production, and the inspected thumbnails contain no display lettering. Therefore no font-style performance conclusion is attributable.

recovery_action: Collect at least four current topic/audience-matched thumbnails using the proposed neutral sans treatment, record each exact public video URL and capture date, then compare age-normalized views with a current same-channel baseline. If no defensible sample exists, retain Unscored.
